# Five things we take on.

::: {.lede .muted}
Sisyphe is small on purpose. One senior engineer, with trusted collaborators when the work needs them, on problems where the model has to meet a real instrument, a real robot, a real signal or a real collection. If you are not sure your problem fits, write anyway.
:::

::: {.offer}

### Robotics, simulation and learned policies
<div class="chips"><span class="chip perceive">perceive</span><span class="chip act">act</span></div>
<div class="evidence">Proof: since 2025 the day job is vision-language-action training pipelines spanning physics simulation, synthetic data, sim-to-real transfer, reinforcement learning and edge deployment. That work is not for hire. Public evidence: mjdrone, a MuJoCo quadrotor simulator that speaks MAVLink so Udacity course flight scripts connect unchanged, headless at 30 to 60 times real time, and a personal sim-to-real project on NVIDIA Cosmos.</div>
</div>
<div>
Simulators that are fast, inspectable and scriptable. Reinforcement learning and vision-language-action policies, and the sim-to-real gap between them and a machine that moves. We build the environment, the training loop and the evaluation that tells you whether the policy learned the task or the simulator.
</div>

## How it works

**Scoped engagements.** A written brief, a fixed number of weeks, a demo at the end. We prefer two to eight weeks with a clear question over open-ended retainers.

**Advisory.** A few hours a month to review architecture, models or an agent design before you commit a team to it.

**Open source first.** If the work belongs in Sideman or a public library, we will say so and price it accordingly.
